narrative.overview: collab_ai is not a dashboard people report to — it's a desk several people sit around, with the AI agent as one more hand on the same document. The visual system already in place backs this up: everyone reads off the same calm, cool-toned surface, the topbar is the one fixed room landmark, and every meaningful state — thinking, awaiting approval, denied, mine — gets a specific, quiet color rather than an alert-style callout. Nothing yells. Status is legible at a glance (a pip, a border color, a dashed outline) so the room can stay focused on the conversation and the document instead of the chrome around them. The palette and type scale are a considered, working system already — cool blue-white surfaces, a single sky-blue accent, tinted state colors (ok/bad/warn) reused consistently for votes, tool results, and diffs. It is not treated as final identity; color values are documented as the current source of truth, not locked doctrine, and may be revisited.
keyCharacteristics: Cool, pale blue-white surfaces at rest; a dark slate topbar as the one fixed landmark
One accent color, reused everywhere action or 'live' state needs to read
Flat by default — structure comes from border + background-tint, not shadow
Every state (ok / bad / warn / mine / auto-accept) has one committed color, reused verbatim
Full parallel dark theme via [data-theme="dark"], not an afterthought

rules.name: The One State, One Color Rule
rules.body: Ok/bad/warn/mine map to exactly one meaning each, reused verbatim across chat, votes, tool results, and diffs.

rules.name: The No-Fade Rule
rules.body: Quiet is a token, never an opacity. --ink-faint is the quietest legible tier and already sits at the contrast floor. Only :disabled may fade, because WCAG exempts it.

rules.name: The Boundary Rule
rules.body: --line divides; --line-strong bounds. If a user can click or type into it and its fill does not separate it from the surface, its border identifies the control and takes --line-strong.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Every weight of hierarchy stays on the Inter stack; distinguish code-like content by size and background tint instead.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from border and background-tint, not shadow. Shadow tokens are reserved for elements that float above the layout, and each has a dark-theme value.

dos: Do reuse the committed semantic colors (ok/bad/warn/mine-line) verbatim for any new approve/deny/warning/own-content state.
Do build new surfaces from border + background-tint (panel/panel-2/panel-3), not shadow.
Do keep new interactive controls at 7px radius and new containing surfaces at 9-10px, reserving pill radius for chips/tags/toggles only.
Do keep the topbar's translucent-white control treatment isolated to the topbar.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface for code/mono content.
Don't add ambient drop-shadows to cards, panels, or modals.
Don't style the topbar's light/dark swap the same as the rest of the app — it intentionally stays a fixed dark surface in both themes.
